claims.text: Northwind Components is a mid-market industrial manufacturer seeking a consulting partner to review and redesign its distribution network across four regional markets.
The scope includes assessing the current distribution centre footprint and outbound logistics cost base.
The scope includes modeling alternative network configurations against service-level and cost constraints.
The scope includes segmenting the supplier base by risk and reducing single-source dependency.
The scope includes delivering an implementation roadmap with a clear inventory policy.
Respondents are asked to evidence comparable network redesign work, describe delivery methodology and team model, and state the firm's geographic delivery footprint.
VCG follows a four-phase delivery methodology: Diagnose, Design, Deliver, Sustain.
A joint steering committee governs every engagement and meets fortnightly.
For engagements longer than six months VCG assigns a dedicated Engagement Quality Director independent of the delivery team.
Knowledge-transfer workshops are conducted in the final four weeks of each engagement.
Leveraging VCG’s presence in 14 markets, local delivery teams can be mobilised within ten business days of contract signature.
The project will apply VCG’s Network Optimiser toolkit to model multiple network scenarios against service-level and cost constraints.
We will evaluate at least 20 alternative distribution network configurations to identify the optimal footprint and logistics cost structure.
VCG segments suppliers using spend concentration, geographic exposure and financial-health signals.
The final deliverable will include an implementation roadmap and a clear inventory policy aligned with the redesigned network.
VCG redesigned Meridian Industrial’s distribution network across four regional distribution centres, reducing outbound logistics cost by 14 percent within 11 months.
The Meridian engagement deployed a six-person team over nine months and used the Network Optimiser toolkit to model 27 scenarios against service-level and cost constraints.
Inventory carrying cost fell 9 percent during the same period for Meridian Industrial.
VCG segmented 1,180 suppliers for Arclight Manufacturing into four risk tiers using spend concentration, geographic exposure and financial-health signals.
Single-source dependency for Arclight was reduced from 23 percent to 9 percent of addressable spend over 14 months.
A supplier early-warning dashboard was handed over to the client’s procurement team at close of the Arclight engagement.
VCG operates across 12 markets.
VCG has delivered 340 engagements since 2020 with an average team size of seven consultants.
VCG’s repeat-engagement rate of 68 percent demonstrates strong client satisfaction and long-term partnership capability.
The four-phase methodology, dedicated quality oversight, and knowledge-transfer workshops ensure rigorous delivery and sustainable outcomes.
Proven network redesign results, such as a 14 percent logistics cost reduction for Meridian, illustrate VCG’s capability to deliver measurable savings.
Supplier risk segmentation experience, reducing single-source dependency from 23 percent to 9 percent, shows VCG can address the RFP’s supplier-risk objective.
Rapid mobilization of local teams within ten business days enables VCG to start the Northwind project quickly across its four regional markets.
VCG’s average engagement team size is seven consultants.
VCG successfully deployed a six-person team for a network redesign engagement.
